title: Choose the visual world of the quickstart page
question: The roll assigned Working Timetable. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Working Timetable
options.lineage: Railway working timetables and their graphic train charts
options.thesis: Each fact is a service on a timetable: it runs from a date, between two stops, on the line of the section that states it.
materials: one line colour for each source section
options.viewport: A deep blue rail on the left holds the conversation and each tool call. The rest of the screen is the result of the selected tool call: the graph of entities and facts at full size, a validity ruler under it, then the fact table and the section texts.
options.risk: Nearly all facts start on 23 July 2021 and have no end date, so the validity ruler shows many equal lines for this Act.

raised.raise: The fact table uses one type size. Weight, case and rules carry the rank.
Each colour has one job. A line colour means one source section and nothing else.
Point at a section colour, and the page shows only the facts of that section in the graph, the table and the ruler.
Data at full density: no field of the result is hidden, and no grey filler stands in for it.

options.label: Notation Sheet
options.lineage: Software specification diagrams: entity boxes, labelled arrows, yellow notes
options.thesis: The result is drawn in the diagram notation that a developer already reads in every design document.
options.viewport: A white sheet. The conversation is a narrow column on the left. The graph fills the right side as a diagram of boxes and labelled arrows, and each arrow has a yellow note with its dates and its section.
options.risk: This is the familiar choice. It can look like the output of any diagram tool.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: A pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size on raked glass slides over a goldenrod bed.
options.viewport: A raked rack of slides, one for each tool call.
options.case: The 11 degree rake makes a table of facts and dates harder to read.
options.kept: One type size in the data table.

options.label: Manual with Acetate Leaves
options.thesis: One strong hue for each division, with the text on clear leaves above it.
options.viewport: A tab rail down the edge, one tab for each tool call.
options.case: It is a reading layout. The graph has no natural place on a leaf.
options.risk: Reads as a document, not a tool.
options.kept: A state change is a short step, with no slow fade.

options.label: Terminal Yellow Wayfinding
options.thesis: Yellow bands with black type that name only the next choice.
options.case: Signs show one choice at a time. The page must show a whole graph at one time.
options.risk: Too little data on the screen.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Dense barcode columns and monospace numbers in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A field of bars with the graph inside.
options.case: You excluded the dark console look and decoration that hides the data.

options.label: Cassette J-card
options.thesis: Ballpoint track lists with running times.
options.viewport: Side A and side B lists.
options.case: Handwriting does not fit a result of a library that must be read exactly.
options.kept: Times aligned to the right edge.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: White line plots on matte black, with colour blocks in place of words.
options.viewport: One plot on a black field.
options.case: It hides labels behind a code, and it is a dark look that you excluded.
options.risk: The reader must decode the page.
options.kept: Pointing at a colour shows its meaning.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A centered chat column with tool result cards inline and a force-directed graph of coloured circles.
canonCard.viewport: A chat in the center. Each tool call is a card in the message list with a small graph inside.
canonCard.risk: You said that a generic AI chat look would feel wrong.
